mentl/f673ea4:
The banked probe ran: wasm-objdump at the address the backtrace named.
Inside parse_int_go, two indirect calls sit three instructions apart — a
call_indirect through ft2 and a return_call_indirect through ft3. The
tail call is the one that traps, and its callee is a closure record's fn
pointer.

The type vocabulary is identical across generations: both carry the same
36-entry table, with ft2 as (i32,i32)->i32 and ft3 as
(i32,i32,i32)->i32. That narrows the fault hard. The mismatch is not a
changed signature but a changed target — after the rename, the closure's
stored fn index resolves to a function of different arity.

An ambient find, and the docs paid for it in this very probe. WABT
1.0.39's wasm-objdump accepts no feature flags at all and disassembles
tail-call-bearing modules fine without them; the flag turned the first
attempt into a two-line "unknown option" before it read a single
instruction. Section 8's "EVERY tool needs" is true of the assembler and
validator and false of objdump at this version, and is trued in place.

No src change, fourth in a row, and the reason named plainly: the row arc
is blocked behind an emitter defect that has nothing to do with rows. A
nested function cannot currently be renamed without an indirect call
resolving to the wrong arity, and every step toward the open-row fix
passes through such a rename. Each iteration's probe has been the loop's
mandated first move and each has advanced the pin one layer — startup
failure, then naming, then instruction, now target versus signature — but
none of them is the fix.

Next probe: read which fn index that closure stores and what occupies it
in each generation. The fns table plus the closure's construction site
answer it, and the answer either names a collision or a stale index.

Boot unchanged; docs only.

The last diagnosed f64 typing root: lower_pat's PCon arm handed every
sub-binder the SCRUTINEE's handle, so f in LFloat(f) => never typed
f64 and its call into the f64-typed float_to_str picked the all-i32
table entry. A seed pattern node carries no handle, so the width
cannot ride the handle channel or the flat per-fn name ledger — the
representation changes instead: LPVar widens to (handle, name, repr),
lower_pat stamps repr from the ConstructorScheme's payload types (the
same kind-132 channel the nominal-record and payload-offset reads
use), and emit's bind ORs the stamp into the unbox guard and ledger.

The collision the design flagged is real, measured: lower_expr_body
binds LitInt(v) and LitFloat(v) in one fn, and one WASM local cannot
hold two widths — so f64 ctor sub-binders mangle deterministically to
name.f64 (a dot cannot appear in a source identifier), applied
identically at bind, scope entry, and every use.

En route, emit_lsuspend's evidence dispatch stops flooring f64 args:
it routes through the typed call_indirect form (all-i32 stays on
$ftN byte-identical; any f64 gets the inline-typed signature) —

mentl/f611794:
Self-hosting stack overflow root cause: str_eq_loop and similar
byte-by-byte recursive functions blew wasmtime's stack at N ≈ 300K-1M
(depending on frame size) because every recursive call allocated a
new WASM frame. Compiling lux3 to produce lux4 hit it; lux4 running
any non-trivial input hit it. Manifested as `wasm trap: call stack
exhausted` with the trace showing only str_eq_loop frames.

Lux's LowIR always had LTailCall as an unused alternative to LCall;
the emission scaffolding was dead code. This commit wires it up at
the emission layer — no checker / lowerer changes, no new
primitives, just structural-truth-seeking emission:

  emit_fn_body → emit_stmts_value_tail (last stmt in tail position)
  emit_stmts_value_tail → emit_expr_tail on last stmt
  emit_expr_tail →
    LCall/LTailCall  → emit_tail_call_expr (return_call /
                       return_call_indirect)
    LIf              → propagate tail into both branches
    LBlock           → propagate tail to last stmt
    else             → fall through to regular emit_expr (non-tail)

  emit_tail_call_expr mirrors emit_call_expr but emits the
  return_* variants for direct/indirect calls. Builtins, tags,
  and closures fall back to regular call — they're intrinsics
  with bespoke emit sequences, not user functions.

Toolchain: wat2wasm / wasm2wat / wasm-validate invocations all now
pass --enable-tail-call. wasmtime 43.0.1 supports the proposal
natively, no flag needed.

Verified:
- Stage0+1 produces lux3.wasm with ~700 return_call instructions
- counter.lux via lux3 → 99 return_call in output, validates, runs
  clean exit 0
